findings.evidence: Functoriality.lean:79-100 (new lemma with `heq` inline at 83-98) versus the existing dual pairs at 69/104, 147/161, 177/208; `grep -rn congrLinearEquiv TauCeti` shows no conjugation-as-transport lemma anywhere in the repo, and Mathlib only provides `congrLinearEquiv_apply` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/GeneralLinearGroup/Basic.lean:115). The unipotent element predicate is a roadmap target (TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups/README.md:179-181).
findings.fix: Extract `heq` as a public lemma in the `Predicates` section (e.g. `conj_eq_congrLinearEquiv (g h : GeneralLinearGroup K V) : h * g * h⁻¹ = LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.congrLinearEquiv h.toLinearEquiv g`), reprove `isSemisimple_conj_iff` from it in two lines, and add the one-line `@[simp] isUnipotent_conj_iff` via `isUnipotent_congrLinearEquiv_iff`; list both in the module docstring.
findings.issue: `isSemisimple_conj_iff` is added with no `isUnipotent_conj_iff`, and its reusable core `heq : h * g * h⁻¹ = LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.congrLinearEquiv h.toLinearEquiv g` (lines 83-98) is a `have` inside the proof, so no consumer can reach it; every other predicate/part in this file comes in a semisimple/unipotent pair.

summary: The new isSemisimple_conj_iff hides its only reusable content — the identity h * g * h⁻¹ = congrLinearEquiv h.toLinearEquiv g — inside its proof and ships without the unipotent dual, in a file whose API is paired throughout. Everything else (hidden bodies, intro/elim across module opacity, private helpers, simp annotations, no compatibility surface) is fine.
